suggestedOps.title: AI suggestions

@suggestedOps.title.description: Title of the dialog listing the file actions (move, trash, rename, and so on) Ask Cmdr has suggested for the user to approve or reject.

suggestedOps.description: The agent suggested the actions below. Apply them only if you agree.

@suggestedOps.description.description: Warning note at the top of the AI suggestions dialog, above the suggested actions: the AI agent made these suggestions, and nothing happens unless the person approves one. It only shows when there is something to approve. The user can close it for good with its × (suggestedOps.approvalNoticeDismiss), and bring it back in Settings > Advanced.

@suggestedOps.approvalNoticeDismiss.description: Tooltip and screen-reader name of the × that closes the note at the top of the AI suggestions dialog (suggestedOps.description) for good. It can be turned back on in Settings > Advanced.

@suggestedOps.sweepWhen.justNow.description: Heading above a batch of AI suggestions made less than a minute ago.

@suggestedOps.sweepWhen.minutesAgo.description: Heading above a batch of AI suggestions made within the last hour. {countText} is the number of whole minutes (1–59), already formatted.

@suggestedOps.sweepWhen.today.description: Heading above a batch of AI suggestions made earlier today. {time} is the time of day in the user's format, for example "14:04" or "2:04 PM".

@suggestedOps.sweepWhen.yesterday.description: Heading above a batch of AI suggestions made yesterday. {time} is the time of day in the user's format, for example "14:04" or "2:04 PM".

@suggestedOps.sweepWhen.earlier.description: Heading above a batch of AI suggestions made before yesterday. {date} is a date and time already formatted in the user's chosen date format, for example "2026-10-20 12:22". {date} always starts with the date (never a weekday or a word like "on").

suggestedOps.empty: Nothing is waiting for you right now.

@suggestedOps.empty.description: Shown in the dialog body when the agent has no pending suggestions.

suggestedOps.loadFailed: Cmdr couldn’t read the suggestions. Close this dialog and open it again.

@suggestedOps.loadFailed.description: Shown when reading the suggestion list threw. Distinct from the empty state, which would read as the agent having suggested nothing.

@suggestedOps.agentReason.description: Bold label leading the AI's own explanation of a suggestion, on the same line as the explanation. Short on purpose; its tooltip (suggestedOps.agentReasonTooltip) and its screen-reader form (suggestedOps.agentReasonSpoken) say the words are the AI's. Keep the colon or your language's equivalent.

suggestedOps.agentReasonTooltip: The AI’s own words. Cmdr didn’t check them.

@suggestedOps.agentReasonTooltip.description: Tooltip on the "Why:" label (suggestedOps.agentReason) before the AI's explanation of a suggestion. Load-bearing: it marks the text as the AI's claim rather than something Cmdr verified.

@suggestedOps.agentReasonSpoken.description: What a screen reader says in place of the visible "Why:" label (suggestedOps.agentReason), before the AI's explanation of a suggestion. It must start with the same words as the visible label (WCAG 2.5.3, label in name), then name the AI as the source, which the short visible label leaves to its tooltip.

@suggestedOps.fileCount.description: How many files a suggestion group covers, beside the group's title.

@suggestedOps.action.move.description: The action a suggestion takes, leading its title in the AI suggestions dialog, before the name the AI gave it (for example "Move Old installers"). This one moves files to another folder. A short VERB phrase in the imperative, like a menu command; it must read as what happens when the person approves.

@suggestedOps.action.copy.description: The action a suggestion takes, leading its title in the AI suggestions dialog, before the name the AI gave it (for example "Copy Old installers"). This one copies files to another folder. A short VERB phrase in the imperative, like a menu command; it must read as what happens when the person approves.

@suggestedOps.action.trash.description: The action a suggestion takes, leading its title in the AI suggestions dialog, before the name the AI gave it (for example "Move to Trash Old installers"). This one moves files to the Trash. Use the same name for the Trash as the macOS Finder does. A short VERB phrase in the imperative, like a menu command; it must read as what happens when the person approves.

@suggestedOps.action.delete.description: The action a suggestion takes, leading its title in the AI suggestions dialog, before the name the AI gave it (for example "Delete Old installers"). This one deletes files permanently, skipping the Trash. A short VERB phrase in the imperative, like a menu command; it must read as what happens when the person approves.

@suggestedOps.action.rename.description: The action a suggestion takes, leading its title in the AI suggestions dialog, before the name the AI gave it (for example "Rename Old installers"). This one renames files in place. A short VERB phrase in the imperative, like a menu command; it must read as what happens when the person approves.

@suggestedOps.action.compress.description: The action a suggestion takes, leading its title in the AI suggestions dialog, before the name the AI gave it (for example "Compress Old installers"). This one packs files into one archive (a zip). A short VERB phrase in the imperative, like a menu command; it must read as what happens when the person approves.

@suggestedOps.action.extract.description: The action a suggestion takes, leading its title in the AI suggestions dialog, before the name the AI gave it (for example "Extract Old installers"). This one unpacks archives (zip files and the like) into a folder. A short VERB phrase in the imperative, like a menu command; it must read as what happens when the person approves.

@suggestedOps.approve.move.description: Primary button on a suggestion that moves files to another folder. Pressing it starts the move. {countText} is how many files would run (the ones the user left ticked), already formatted.

@suggestedOps.approve.copy.description: Primary button on a suggestion that copies files to another folder. Pressing it starts the copy. {countText} is how many files would run, already formatted.

suggestedOps.approve.trash: Move {countText} {count, plural, one {file} other {files}} to Trash

@suggestedOps.approve.trash.description: Primary button on a suggestion that moves files to the Trash. Use the same name for the Trash as the macOS Finder does in your language. {countText} is how many files would run, already formatted.

@suggestedOps.approve.delete.description: Primary button on a suggestion that deletes files permanently (not to the Trash). {countText} is how many files would run, already formatted.

@suggestedOps.approve.rename.description: Primary button on a suggestion that renames files in place. {countText} is how many files would run, already formatted.

@suggestedOps.approve.compress.description: Primary button on a suggestion that packs files into one archive (a zip). {countText} is how many files would go in, already formatted.

@suggestedOps.approve.extract.description: Primary button on a suggestion that unpacks archives (zip files and the like) into a folder. {countText} is how many archives would be unpacked, already formatted.

@suggestedOps.approve.addServer.description: Primary button on a suggestion to save a new server (a NAS, an SFTP or WebDAV server, and the like) in Cmdr's server list. Pressing it saves the server without connecting to it. Takes no count. It sits on the same card as the suggestedOps.server.add tag, so keep the two worded differently.

@suggestedOps.approve.editServer.description: Primary button on a suggestion to change the settings of a server already saved in Cmdr's server list (its name, folder, or account). Pressing it saves the changes. Takes no count.

@suggestedOps.reject.description: Button that turns one suggestion down. Nothing happens to the files.

@suggestedOps.facts.from.description: Short label before the folder the suggested files are in now, in the fact lines under a suggestion's title. Followed by a folder path. The label sits in its own column with no colon or other separator after it, the way Finder's Get Info labels do.

@suggestedOps.facts.to.description: Short label before where the files would go (a drive name and a folder path, or the Trash), in the fact lines under a suggestion's title. The label sits in its own column with no colon or other separator after it.

@suggestedOps.facts.folder.description: Short label before the folder whose files a rename suggestion would rename in place. Followed by a folder path.

@suggestedOps.facts.archive.description: Short label before the archive file (for example a .zip) a compress suggestion would create. Followed by a drive name and a file path.

@suggestedOps.facts.trash.description: Shown after the "To" label (suggestedOps.facts.to) when the suggestion moves files to the Trash. Use the same name for the Trash as the macOS Finder does in your language.

@suggestedOps.facts.severalFolders.description: Shown after the "From" label (suggestedOps.facts.from) when the suggested files sit in different folders, so there's no one folder to name. Each file's folder then shows in the list.

suggestedOps.reversible.trash: You can undo this: {count, plural, one {it goes} other {they go}} to the Trash

@suggestedOps.reversible.trash.description: Note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on a suggestion that moves files to the Trash, saying the user can take it back and why. {count} is the number of files, only used to pick "it" or "they". Use the same name for the Trash as the macOS Finder does. "It" and "they" are the suggested files; a language that needs a noun can say "the file" / "the files". The items can be files or folders.

suggestedOps.reversible.moveBack: You can undo this: Cmdr can move {count, plural, one {it} other {them}} back

@suggestedOps.reversible.moveBack.description: Note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on a suggestion that moves files, saying the user can take it back because Cmdr can move the files back where they were. {count} only picks "it" or "them". The items can be files or folders.

suggestedOps.reversible.renameBack: You can undo this: Cmdr can change the {count, plural, one {name} other {names}} back

@suggestedOps.reversible.renameBack.description: Note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on a rename suggestion, saying the user can take it back because Cmdr can restore the old names. {count} only picks "name" or "names".

suggestedOps.reversible.removeCopies: You can undo this: Cmdr deletes the copies

@suggestedOps.reversible.removeCopies.description: Note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on a copy suggestion, saying the user can take it back: undoing deletes the copies it made, and the originals were never touched.

suggestedOps.reversible.removeArchive: You can undo this: Cmdr deletes the new archive

@suggestedOps.reversible.removeArchive.description: Note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on a compress suggestion that creates a new archive file, saying the user can take it back: undoing deletes the archive, and the original files were never touched.

suggestedOps.reversible.removeExtracted: You can undo this: Cmdr deletes what it extracted

@suggestedOps.reversible.removeExtracted.description: Note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on an extract suggestion, saying the user can take it back: undoing deletes the unpacked files, and the archives themselves were never touched.

suggestedOps.irreversible.delete: This can’t be undone: the files are deleted for good

@suggestedOps.irreversible.delete.description: Warning note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on a suggestion that deletes files permanently, skipping the Trash. Disclosure only: the user can still approve it.

@suggestedOps.noTrash.description: Pill beside the title of a suggestion to move files to the Trash when the files are on a drive or server that keeps no Trash. The suggestion then deletes the files permanently instead, and its title and button say "Delete". Use the same name for the Trash as the macOS Finder does. The tooltip is suggestedOps.noTrashTooltip.

suggestedOps.noTrashTooltip: The drive these files are on keeps no Trash, so approving this deletes them for good.

@suggestedOps.noTrashTooltip.description: Tooltip on the suggestedOps.noTrash pill. Use the same name for the Trash as the macOS Finder does.

suggestedOps.irreversible.overwrite: This can’t be undone: it replaces an existing archive

@suggestedOps.irreversible.overwrite.description: Warning note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on a compress suggestion whose archive file already exists, so approving overwrites it and the old archive is gone.

@suggestedOps.irreversible.other.description: Warning note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on a suggestion nothing can take back, when there's no more specific reason to give. Disclosure only: the user can still approve it.

suggestedOps.reversible.forgetServer: You can undo this: forget the server in Servers

@suggestedOps.reversible.forgetServer.description: Note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on a suggestion to save a new server, saying the user can take it back: they can remove (forget) the saved server again in the Servers view. Same “You can undo this:” frame as the other suggestedOps.reversible.* pills. “Forget” is the word on the menu item that removes a saved server (menu.network.forgetServer), so use the same word your translation uses there. "Servers" is the name of that view in Cmdr; translate it the same way as there.

suggestedOps.reversible.changeServerBack: You can undo this: change the server back in Servers

@suggestedOps.reversible.changeServerBac.description: Note under a suggestion’s file list, beside its buttons on a suggestion to change a saved server's settings, saying the user can take it back by editing the server again in the Servers view. Same “You can undo this:” frame as the other suggestedOps.reversible.* pills. “Change the server back” means putting its settings back the way they were. "Servers" is the name of that view in Cmdr; translate it the same way as there.

@suggestedOps.folderWillBeCreated.description: Shown beside the target folder’s path, after a folder-with-a-plus icon, when that folder doesn’t exist yet.

suggestedOps.folderWillBeCreatedTooltip: The target folder is not there yet. Approving creates it, exactly as it would if you started the move yourself.
suggestedOps.destinationUnknown: Cmdr couldn’t check the target folder

@suggestedOps.destinationUnknown.description: Shown beside the target folder’s path when the destination drive or server didn’t answer in time, so whether the folder exists is genuinely unknown rather than assumed.

@suggestedOps.destinationNotConnected.description: Shown beside the target folder’s path when the target is on a saved server, share, or phone that Cmdr hasn’t connected to yet, so it couldn’t look at the folder. The tooltip is suggestedOps.destinationNotConnectedTooltip.

suggestedOps.destinationNotConnectedTool: Cmdr hasn’t connected to this drive or server yet. Approving won’t start until it’s connected, the same as when you move files there yourself.

@suggestedOps.destinationNotConnectedToo.description: Tooltip on the pill saying a suggestion’s target drive or server isn’t connected (suggestedOps.destinationNotConnected).

@suggestedOps.fromPattern.description: Pill on a suggestion whose file list a pattern produced, so the user knows the list was matched rather than named one by one.

suggestedOps.changedUnderReview: The AI changed this suggestion while you were reading it.

@suggestedOps.changedUnderReview.description: Notice shown when the agent amended a suggestion the user is looking at. The rows on screen stay put until the user asks for the new version.

@suggestedOps.showNewVersion.description: Button that reloads a suggestion the agent changed while the user was reading it.

@suggestedOps.filesLabel.description: Accessible name of one suggestion's file list, read by screen readers. {name} is the suggestion's title. Use your language's quotation marks.

@suggestedOps.columnInclude.description: Screen-reader-only heading of the tick-box column in a suggestion's file list. A ticked file is part of the approval.

@suggestedOps.includeAll.description: Screen-reader name of the tick box in the header of a suggestion's file list. Ticking it includes every file in the approval, unticking it includes none; it shows a dash when only some are ticked.

@suggestedOps.columnName.description: Column heading for the name of each file a suggestion would touch.

@suggestedOps.columnFolder.description: Column heading for the folder each file is in. Only shown when a suggestion's files sit in different folders.

@suggestedOps.columnNewName.description: Screen-reader text between a file's current name and the name a suggestion would give it, read as "invoice.pdf, New name, Invoice 2026-07.pdf". Visually an arrow stands in for it. A short noun phrase.

@suggestedOps.columnSize.description: Column heading for each file's size as Cmdr finds it on disk now.

@suggestedOps.columnModified.description: Column heading for when each file was last changed, as Cmdr finds it on disk now.

@suggestedOps.factChanged.description: Screen-reader name of a small warning glyph beside a file's size or date when the value on disk now differs from what it was when the AI made the suggestion. The tooltip (suggestedOps.factChangedTooltip) shows both values.

@suggestedOps.factChangedTooltip.description: Tooltip on the warning glyph beside a file's size or date that changed since the AI made the suggestion. {then} and {now} are both sizes (like "1.2 MB") or both dates, already formatted.

@suggestedOps.fileMissing.description: Shown in a file's Size column when the file isn't where the suggestion says any more: something moved or deleted it since. Approving skips it. The row can be a file or a folder.

suggestedOps.snapshotOnly: From when the AI suggested this

@suggestedOps.snapshotOnly.description: Screen-reader name of a small clock glyph beside a file's size or date when Cmdr couldn't look at the file just now, so the value is what it was when the AI made the suggestion. The tooltip is suggestedOps.snapshotOnlyTooltip.

suggestedOps.snapshotOnlyTooltip: Cmdr couldn’t check this file just now, so this is what it was when the AI suggested it.

@suggestedOps.snapshotOnlyTooltip.description: Tooltip on the clock glyph beside a file's size or date that Cmdr couldn't check live, explaining the value is from suggestion time.

suggestedOps.sourceNotConnected: Cmdr isn’t connected to the drive these files are on, so their sizes and dates are from when the AI suggested this.

@suggestedOps.sourceNotConnected.description: Note above a suggestion's file list when the files sit on a saved server, share, or phone Cmdr hasn't connected to, so it couldn't look at them now. The sizes and dates shown are the ones recorded when the AI made the suggestion. "Dates" means the files' last-modified dates, not data.

suggestedOps.sourceGone: The drive these files were on isn’t here any more, so their sizes and dates are from when the AI suggested this.

@suggestedOps.sourceGone.description: Note above a suggestion's file list when the drive or server holding the files was disconnected or removed, so Cmdr couldn't look at them now. The sizes and dates shown are the ones recorded when the AI made the suggestion. "Dates" means the files' last-modified dates, not data.

@suggestedOps.factUnknown.description: Shown in a file's Size or Last modified column when Cmdr has no value at all: it couldn't check the file now and recorded nothing when the AI made the suggestion. Never a zero, which would read as an empty file. The same string stands in for either a size or a date, so in a gendered language pick a form that reads right for both (or a neutral one).

@suggestedOps.includeFile.description: Screen-reader name of the tick box on each file row. Ticked means the file is part of the approval. {name} is the file's name.

@suggestedOps.showMore.description: Button under a suggestion's file list that shows the next few files. {countText} is how many it adds, already formatted.

@suggestedOps.showAll.description: Button under a suggestion's file list that shows every file. {countText} is the total number of files, already formatted (it can be tens of thousands).

@suggestedOps.loadingFiles.description: Shown while the suggestions or a page of a file list are being read.

@suggestedOps.filesLoadFailed.description: Shown above a suggestion's file list when reading its files didn't work. It takes the place of the per-row loading placeholder, which would otherwise wait forever. The button beside it is suggestedOps.retryFiles.

@suggestedOps.retryFiles.description: Button beside suggestedOps.filesLoadFailed that reads the suggestion's files again. A short control label.

suggestedOps.decisionNotRecorded: Cmdr couldn’t save your answer. Try again.

@suggestedOps.decisionNotRecorded.description: Notice at the top of the AI suggestions dialog when pressing the approve button or Reject didn't reach the suggestion store, so nothing changed. The list has just been reloaded, so every suggestion shows as it really stands, and the person presses the same button again.

suggestedOps.approvalUnsure: Cmdr isn’t sure the approval went through. Check the operation queue before you approve it again.

@suggestedOps.approvalUnsure.description: Notice at the top of the AI suggestions dialog when an approval stopped answering partway, so whether its files started moving is unknown. "Operation queue" names the queue window by its title (queue.windowTitle); keep the two matching. The point is to stop the person running the same files twice.

suggestedOps.refusal.label: Why this didn’t start

@suggestedOps.refusal.label.description: Small label above the reason shown under a suggestion whose approval didn't start. The suggestion is back on the list as waiting, nothing ran, and the person can approve or reject it again. The reason itself sits below this label.

suggestedOps.refusal.nothingToRun.messag: Cmdr couldn’t read any of these files when you approved, so nothing ran.

@suggestedOps.refusal.nothingToRun.messa.description: Reason shown under a suggestion whose approval didn't start because every file it names was gone or unreadable at that moment. The suggestion is back on the list, waiting for an answer. Followed by suggestedOps.refusal.nothingToRun.suggestion.

suggestedOps.refusal.nothingToRun.sugges: Check that they’re still there, then approve it again, or reject it.

@suggestedOps.refusal.nothingToRun.sugge.description: What to do next, under suggestedOps.refusal.nothingToRun.message. "It" is the suggestion; the approve button and Reject are on it.

suggestedOps.refusal.nothingSelected.mes: None of the files you ticked are in this suggestion any more, so nothing ran.

@suggestedOps.refusal.nothingSelected.me.description: Reason shown under a suggestion whose approval didn't start because none of the files the person had ticked were still part of it (the AI changed the suggestion in the meantime). The suggestion is back on the list. Followed by suggestedOps.refusal.nothingSelected.suggestion.

suggestedOps.refusal.nothingSelected.sug: Tick the files you want, then approve it again.

@suggestedOps.refusal.nothingSelected.su.description: What to do next, under suggestedOps.refusal.nothingSelected.message. "It" is the suggestion; the tick boxes are on each file row and the approve button is on the suggestion.

suggestedOps.refusal.couldNotStart.messa: Cmdr couldn’t turn this suggestion into an operation, so nothing ran.

@suggestedOps.refusal.couldNotStart.mess.description: Reason shown under a suggestion whose approval didn't start because the stored suggestion itself was incomplete (rare, an internal inconsistency). The suggestion is back on the list, waiting for an answer. Followed by suggestedOps.refusal.couldNotStart.suggestion.

suggestedOps.refusal.couldNotStart.sugge: Reject it, and ask Cmdr to suggest it again.

@suggestedOps.refusal.couldNotStart.sugg.description: What to do next, under suggestedOps.refusal.couldNotStart.message. "It" is the suggestion; Reject is the button on it. "Ask Cmdr to" means asking in the Ask Cmdr chat, the same phrasing as the other suggestedOps.refusal.*.suggestion keys.

@suggestedOps.refusal.serverLabel.description: Small label above the reason shown under a suggestion to add or change a server, when pressing its button saved nothing. The suggestion is back on the list as waiting, and the person can approve or reject it again. The reason itself sits below this label. Counterpart of suggestedOps.refusal.label for file suggestions.

suggestedOps.refusal.serverChanged.messa: This server changed since the AI suggested this, so Cmdr saved nothing.

@suggestedOps.refusal.serverChanged.mess.description: Reason shown under a suggestion to change a saved server's settings, when the saved server itself was changed (by the person, or by another approved suggestion) after the AI suggested this. Saving would overwrite a change the suggestion doesn't show, so nothing was saved. Followed by suggestedOps.refusal.serverChanged.suggestion.

suggestedOps.refusal.serverChanged.sugge: Ask Cmdr to suggest it again, or edit the server in Servers.

@suggestedOps.refusal.serverChanged.sugg.description: What to do next, under suggestedOps.refusal.serverChanged.message. "Ask Cmdr to" means asking in the Ask Cmdr chat, the same phrasing as the other suggestedOps.refusal.*.suggestion keys; "Servers" is the name of the view listing saved servers, translated the same way as there.

suggestedOps.refusal.alreadySaved.messag: This server is already in your servers list, so Cmdr saved nothing.

@suggestedOps.refusal.alreadySaved.messa.description: Reason shown under a suggestion to add a server, when a server at the same address was saved after the AI suggested this (by the person, or by another approved suggestion). Adding it again would replace that one's settings, so nothing was saved. Followed by suggestedOps.refusal.alreadySaved.suggestion.

suggestedOps.refusal.alreadySaved.sugges: Open it from Servers, or ask Cmdr to suggest a change to it instead.

@suggestedOps.refusal.alreadySaved.sugge.description: What to do next, under suggestedOps.refusal.alreadySaved.message. "It" is the server already saved; "ask Cmdr to" means asking in the Ask Cmdr chat, the same phrasing as the other suggestedOps.refusal.*.suggestion keys; "Servers" is the name of the view listing saved servers, translated the same way as there.

suggestedOps.refusal.nameTaken.message: Another saved server is already called {name}, so Cmdr saved nothing.

@suggestedOps.refusal.nameTaken.message.description: Reason shown under a suggestion to add or rename a server, when another saved server took the same name after the AI suggested this. Two servers with one name could be mistaken for each other, so nothing was saved. Followed by suggestedOps.refusal.nameTaken.suggestion.

placeholders.name: the name the other saved server already has, like Naspolya; never translated

suggestedOps.refusal.nameTaken.suggestio: Ask Cmdr to suggest another name.

@suggestedOps.refusal.nameTaken.suggesti.description: What to do next, under suggestedOps.refusal.nameTaken.message. "Ask Cmdr to" means asking in the Ask Cmdr chat, the same phrasing as the other suggestedOps.refusal.*.suggestion keys.

@suggestedOps.server.add.description: Leads the title of a suggestion to save a new server (a NAS, an SFTP or WebDAV server, and the like) in Cmdr’s server list, before the server’s name. It names the action, like the suggestedOps.action.* keys do for file suggestions; the button on the same card is suggestedOps.approve.addServer, so keep the two worded differently.

@suggestedOps.server.change.description: Leads the title of a suggestion to change the settings of a server already saved in Cmdr’s server list, before the server’s name. It means editing that server’s settings, not swapping it for another server. It names the action, like the suggestedOps.action.* keys do for file suggestions.

@suggestedOps.server.field.port.description: Label of a row on a suggestion to add or change a server: the network port number Cmdr connects to. One word, NOUN.

@suggestedOps.server.field.account.description: Label of a row on a suggestion to add or change a server: the account (username) Cmdr signs in as, or for an S3 server, the saved S3 account it belongs to. One word, NOUN.

@suggestedOps.server.field.share.description: Label of a row on a suggestion to add an SMB server (a NAS, a Windows PC): the shared folder on it that Cmdr saves. NOUN phrase, the network-share term (not the Share menu verb); use the term Finder and Windows use for a network share.

@suggestedOps.server.field.bucket.description: Label of a row on a suggestion to add an S3 server: the S3 bucket Cmdr saves. One word, NOUN; "bucket" is the S3 term, keep the one S3 providers use in your language.

@suggestedOps.server.notSet.description: Shown in place of a value on a suggestion to change a server, when a setting had no value before, or the change clears it (a start folder back to the default). It stands in for any field (a port, a folder, an account), so it can't agree with one noun's gender: pick a form that needs no agreement, like “no value”. Short.

@suggestedOps.server.changesTo.description: Read by screen readers only, between a server setting's old value and its new one on a suggestion to change a server ("/srv, changes to, /srv/backups"). Sighted people see an arrow instead. Lowercase, VERB phrase.

@suggestedOps.server.newAddress.description: Small tag beside the address on a suggestion to add a server, when no server Cmdr has saved is at that address. It warns that the AI is pointing at a place the person hasn't used in Cmdr before. Three words, NOUN phrase. The tooltip is suggestedOps.server.newAddressTooltip.

suggestedOps.server.newAddressTooltip: None of your saved servers is at this address. Check that it’s the one you mean.

@suggestedOps.server.newAddressTooltip.description: Tooltip on the "A new address" tag (suggestedOps.server.newAddress) beside a suggested server's address.

suggestedOps.server.sharesAffected: This changes {countText} saved {count, plural, one {share} other {shares}} on this server.

@suggestedOps.server.sharesAffected.description: Line on a suggestion to change an SMB server (a NAS, a Windows PC), under its settings: the change applies to the whole server, so it reaches every shared folder saved under it. Counted when the dialog opened.

placeholders.countText: the number of shares, already formatted for the locale

suggestedOps.indicatorTooltip: AI suggestions are waiting. Click to review them.

@suggestedOps.indicatorTooltip.description: Tooltip and screen-reader text for the status-corner indicator that opens the AI suggestions dialog. The number itself is in the badge beside it, so the sentence doesn't repeat it. A screen reader reads this sentence, then the number ("AI suggestions are waiting. Click to review them. 3").

@suggestedOps.newNameTaken.description: Screen-reader name of a small warning glyph beside the new name a suggestion gives a file, when a file or folder with that name is already where the file would land. The tooltip is suggestedOps.newNameTakenTooltip.

@suggestedOps.newNameTakenTooltip.description: Tooltip on the warning glyph beside a suggested new name that is already taken where the file would land (the target folder, or the file’s own folder for a rename). {name} is that new name, never translated. Use your language’s quotation marks.
